title: Deborah’s song calls Israel’s leaders and travellers to bless the Lord
speaker: Deborah and Barak (victory song)
recipient: the mighty ones of the people, riders and those in carriages
note: Outside candidate list for 5:9 (‘bless the Lord!’). Repeats the 5:2 call proposed under P00603; 5:3 and 5:12 are Study Context.

title: Gideon asks the messenger for a sign and to await his offering
speaker: Gideon
note: The request for a sign (6:17) opens the same speech; extend the reference to 6:17–18.

title: Joash refuses to surrender Gideon and lets Baal defend himself
speaker: Joash
recipient: the men of the city demanding Gideon’s death
note: Counter-ruling to the recorded demand (6:30): whoever pleads for Baal shall die; ‘if he is a god, he himself shall avenge’.

title: Gideon summons Abiezer and sends messengers to rally four tribes
speaker: Gideon
recipient: Abiezer and the men of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun and Naphtali
note: Outside candidate list. Reported muster by trumpet and messengers. Candidate 6:39 is a petition to God and needs nothing.

title: The Lord has Gideon dismiss the fearful and sort the drinkers
speaker: the Lord
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list. 7:5 gives the test itself (set apart those who lap like dogs). Candidate 7:13 is narrative.

title: Gideon tells the three hundred to copy him and blow trumpets
speaker: Gideon
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Battle orders: ‘as I do, so shall you do’; sound the trumpets around the camp and cry ‘For the Lord and for Gideon!’

title: Gideon asks Succoth for bread for his exhausted men
speaker: Gideon
note: Same request made to Penuel (8:8); both refuse and are punished (8:16–17).

title: Israel asks Gideon to rule; he answers that the Lord will rule
speaker: the men of Israel; Gideon replies
note: Offer of hereditary rule and Gideon’s refusal; the earring request (8:24) is recorded separately.

title: Jotham’s fable warns that treachery in choosing a ruler brings ruin
speaker: Jotham
note: Fable verses 9:8–9, 11, 13–15 are uncovered (9:10, 9:12 are Study Context); extending lets the Wisdom record span fable and application.

title: Gaal incites Shechem against Abimelech and dares him to come out
speaker: Gaal son of Abed
note: Incitement to revolt (‘why should we serve him?’) with a taunt; Zebul’s answering challenge (9:38) is recorded.

title: Abimelech orders his men to cut branches as he did
speaker: Abimelech
note: ‘What you have seen me do, do quickly as I have done’; they burn the stronghold of Shechem’s Tower (9:49).

title: Gilead’s rulers promise headship to whoever leads against Ammon
speaker: the rulers of Gilead’s people
note: Public offer of leadership, fulfilled when the elders enlist Jephthah as head (AUD-07-11-8).

title: Jephthah sends envoys to rebut Ammon’s claim to Gilead
speaker: Jephthah
recipient: the king of the sons of Ammon, through messengers
note: Two embassies (11:12, 11:14–27); Ammon’s demand (11:13) is recorded but Jephthah’s reply, ending ‘May the Lord judge’, is not.

title: Jephthah vows to offer whoever first meets him on his return
speaker: Jephthah
note: Binding vow later carried out (11:35, 39: ‘I cannot turn back’); compare C0930. Addressed to God, hence medium.

title: Jephthah’s daughter bids him keep his vow and asks time to mourn
speaker: Jephthah’s daughter
note: Outside candidate list. 11:36 ‘do to me according to what has gone out from your mouth’ opens the same speech.

title: Israel’s daughters lament Jephthah’s daughter four days every year
speaker: the narrator (an ordinance in Israel)
note: Outside candidate list. Narrated ‘ordinance in Israel’, comparable to the recorded statute at 1 Samuel 30:24–25 (ot-1-samuel-v30-24).

title: Gilead’s guards make Ephraimite fugitives say the password at the fords
speaker: the men of Gilead
recipient: Ephraimite fugitives at the Jordan crossings
note: The Shibboleth test (‘Please say Password’); only the fugitives’ request to cross (12:5) is recorded.

title: The messenger forbids a razor on the promised Nazirite child’s head
speaker: the Lord’s messenger
note: Not covered by the diet records (13:4, 13:7, 13:13–14). Samson restates it at 16:17: link as Additional Scripture.

title: Manoah urges the messenger to stay for a meal of goat
speaker: Manoah
note: Hospitality request, like Gideon’s recorded request to the messenger (ot-judges-v6-18).

title: The messenger declines food and directs the offering to the Lord
speaker: the Lord’s messenger
note: ‘If you prepare a whole burnt offering, offer it to the Lord’; compare ot-judges-v6-20. Manoah obeys (13:19).

title: Samson sets the terms of his wedding riddle wager
speaker: Samson
note: Outside candidate list. 14:12 states Samson’s side of the wager; the recorded 14:13 states theirs.

title: The Timnite men threaten Samson’s wife into coaxing out the riddle
speaker: the men of Timnah (Samson’s companions)
note: Outside candidate list. Coercive order (‘Deceive your husband… lest we burn you’); compare the Delilah commission (AUD-07-16-5).

title: Samson asks Judah’s men to swear they will not kill him
speaker: Samson; the men of Judah swear
recipient: the three thousand men of Judah
note: 15:13 gives the oath sworn in reply (‘we will only bind you… and surely not kill you’). Other candidates here are threats and narrative.

title: Samson asks his guide to let him feel the pillars
speaker: Samson
recipient: the boy leading him by the hand
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Request setting up the temple’s collapse; the boy complies. The prayer in 16:28 is addressed to God.

title: Micah’s mother consecrates the silver to make a carved and cast image
speaker: Micah’s mother
note: Dedication for an idol, carried out through the caster (17:4); recording it implies no approval. Her blessing (17:2) needs nothing.

title: The Danite scouts ask Micah’s priest to inquire of God
speaker: the five Danite scouts
note: Request answered by the priest’s recorded send-off (18:6, Study Context).

title: The Danite scouts urge their tribe to attack Laish
speaker: the five Danite scouts
recipient: their tribe at Zorah and Eshtaol
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 18:10 completes the scouts’ exhortation (a spacious land; ‘God has delivered it into your hands’).

title: The scouts point out Micah’s idols and tell the Danites to decide
speaker: the five Danite scouts
note: ‘Now consider what you shall do’ prompts the seizure of the ephod and images (18:17–18).

title: The woman’s father asks the Levite to eat and stay the night
speaker: the young woman’s father
note: Same fourth-day hospitality: after the meal he presses the Levite to lodge another night (19:6–7).

title: The woman’s father urges the Levite to stay another day and night
speaker: the young woman’s father
note: The fifth-day urging continues: ‘Lodge here today also… tomorrow you may rise early’ (19:9).

title: The servant proposes lodging in Jebus, and the Levite refuses
speaker: the Levite’s servant; his master replies
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Proposal and refusal before the recorded plan for Gibeah or Ramah (19:13); compare the paired proposals at ot-1-samuel-v9-5.

title: The host pleads with the mob and offers two women instead
speaker: the old man, master of the house
note: 19:23 (‘please do not act wickedly… do not commit this folly’) opens the plea that 19:24 completes.

title: The Levite calls Israel to deliberate over what happened at Gibeah
speaker: the Levite
recipient: the sons of Israel assembled at Mizpah
note: He repeats his call for word and counsel before the assembly at Mizpah; link as Additional Scripture.

title: Israel demands that Benjamin hand over Gibeah’s guilty men
speaker: Israel’s tribes, through messengers
note: ‘Hand over the impious men… and remove wickedness from Israel’ echoes the Deuteronomic purge formula; Benjamin refuses.

title: Israel arranges a smoke signal with the ambush at Gibeah
speaker: the men of Israel
note: 20:38 is outside the candidate list. A prearranged battle signal, like recorded signal instructions (ot-1-samuel-v20-21).

title: Israel swears that none will give a daughter to Benjamin
speaker: the men of Israel at Mizpah
note: Communal oath restated at 21:7 and with a curse at 21:18 (link both); it drives the Jabesh and Shiloh measures.

title: Israel’s congregation sends to Benjamin at Rimmon offering peace
speaker: the whole congregation of Israel
recipient: the Benjaminite survivors at the rock of Rimmon
note: Outside candidate list. Reported call to peace. Candidates 21:16–18 are deliberation; their oath is noted under P00653.

title: Israel’s leaders tell the Benjaminites to seize wives at Shiloh
speaker: the elders of the congregation
note: 21:22 completes the instruction: the elders will answer the fathers’ complaints (‘Have mercy on them’).

title: Naomi urges her daughters-in-law to return home because she has no sons
speaker: Naomi
note: Outside candidate list. 1:13 (‘No, my daughters’) ends the same appeal; 1:15 is already linked.

title: Ruth asks to stay with Naomi and pledges loyalty under oath
speaker: Ruth
note: 1:17 completes Ruth’s pledge (‘where you die, I will die’) with her self-curse oath.

title: Naomi advises Ruth to keep with Boaz’s maidens for safety
speaker: Naomi
note: Counsel lest Ruth be molested in another field; Ruth follows it (2:23). The blessings in 2:19–20 need nothing.

title: Naomi prepares Ruth to approach Boaz at the threshing floor
speaker: Naomi
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 3:1–2 open Naomi’s plan (seeking rest for Ruth; Boaz winnows tonight).

title: Ruth asks Boaz to spread his garment over her as redeemer
speaker: Ruth
note: Ruth’s request for marriage and redemption, the hinge of the book; Boaz’s reply is recorded at 3:13.

title: Boaz reassures Ruth, asks her to stay, and promises redemption
speaker: Boaz
note: 3:11 (‘do not be afraid; I will do for you all that you say’) begins the reply recorded at 3:13.

title: Boaz calls the nearer kinsman to redeem Naomi’s field or decline
speaker: Boaz
note: ‘Acquire it before… the elders… if not, tell me’; the marriage condition (4:5) and his refusal (4:6) are recorded.

title: Boaz calls the elders and people to witness his redemption
speaker: Boaz
recipient: the elders and all the people at the gate
note: 4:9 is outside the candidate list. The people answer ‘We are witnesses’ (4:11); the elders’ blessing needs nothing.

title: Hannah vows her son to the Lord as a lifelong Nazirite
speaker: Hannah
note: Vow with Nazirite terms (no wine, no razor), fulfilled at 1:24–28; addressed to God, hence medium.

title: Hannah presents Samuel at Shiloh, lending him to the Lord for life
speaker: Hannah
note: 1:27–28 are outside the candidate list: the dedication fulfilling her vow (1:11) places Samuel in the Lord’s service at Shiloh.

title: No one can intercede for a person who sins against the Lord
speaker: Eli
note: Maxim closing Eli’s rebuke (ot-1-samuel-v2-24; the uncovered 2:23 opens it). Compare the separately recorded maxim at 15:22 (AUD-09-15-22).

title: Appoint Aaron and his sons to the priesthood
speaker: the Lord through a man of God
note: Recalls the choice of Aaron’s house as priests; its second half recalls the priests’ portions (AUD-04-18-8).

title: God honours those who honour him; those who despise him are dishonoured
speaker: the Lord through a man of God
note: Outside candidate list. A declarative principle within the oracle against Eli’s house; the surrounding judgments need nothing.

title: Ashdod rejects the ark, and the rulers send it to Gath
speaker: the men of Ashdod; the Philistine rulers
note: 5:7 (‘The ark… must not stay with us’) is the resolution that convenes the rulers in 5:8. 5:5 is narrated custom.

title: The priests prescribe gold seats and mice and warn against hardened hearts
speaker: the Philistine priests and diviners
note: 6:4 prescribes the five gold seats that the 6:5 record omits; 6:6 warns against hardening hearts like Pharaoh.

title: Samuel appoints his sons as judges over Israel
speaker: Samuel
note: Reported appointment, like other recorded appointments (AUD-11-4-7); the sons’ corruption prompts the demand for a king (8:3–5).

title: Israel’s elders ask Samuel to appoint a king to judge them
speaker: the elders of Israel
note: 8:5 holds the elders’ actual request (‘Now appoint a king over us’); 8:6 only restates it.

title: Israel asks Samuel for a king to judge them
speaker: the people
note: The people renew the demand after Samuel’s warning (‘There must be a king over us’); link as Additional Scripture.

title: Saul and his servant plan to consult the seer with a gift
speaker: Saul and his young servant
note: 9:7–8 continue the same exchange (what to bring; the servant’s quarter-shekel), between the 9:5–6 and 9:9–10 records.

title: Samuel invites Saul to eat and says the donkeys are found
speaker: Samuel
note: 9:20 continues the reply: ‘do not set your heart on them’. Saul’s question about the seer’s house (9:18) needs nothing.

title: Samuel anoints Saul as ruler over the Lord’s people
speaker: Samuel, acting for the Lord
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Only the Lord’s order to anoint (9:16) is recorded, not the anointing and charge to save Israel; 11:15 reports a second anointing.

title: Samuel tells Saul to act as occasion serves once the signs come
speaker: Samuel
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: ‘Do everything your hand finds, for God is with you’; lies between the recorded directions at 10:3–4 and 10:8.

title: Samuel summons Israel to Mizpah to present themselves by tribe
speaker: Samuel
note: 10:17 reports the summons to Mizpah and 10:18 the Lord’s word prefacing the order. The uncle’s question (10:15) needs nothing.

title: Samuel declares the kingship’s rights and lays the scroll before the Lord
speaker: Samuel
note: Outside candidate list. Written ordinance of the kingship, contents unstated; compare the king’s law (C1065). The acclamation in 10:24 needs nothing.

title: Nahash demands every right eye as the price of a treaty
speaker: Nahash the Ammonite
note: Cruel surrender terms between the recorded requests of Jabesh (11:1, 11:3).

title: The people demand death for those who scorned Saul
speaker: the people
note: Demand refused by Saul (11:13); compare the recorded demand for Gideon’s death (ot-judges-v6-30).

title: Saul forbids any execution on the day of the Lord’s deliverance
speaker: Saul
note: Royal clemency comparable to David’s (AUD-10-19-22, 2 Samuel 19:22–24).

title: Samuel calls Israel to Gilgal, where Saul is anointed king
speaker: Samuel
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list. 11:15 reports the outcome: Samuel anointed Saul king before the Lord at Gilgal.

title: Israel asks Samuel for a king to judge them
speaker: the people, as recalled by Samuel
note: Samuel recalls the demand (‘No! A king must reign over us’); link as Additional Scripture. 12:10 is a prayer.

title: Samuel makes obeying the Lord the condition for people and king
speaker: Samuel
note: Covenant terms: fear, serve and obey the Lord and do not rebel, or his hand will be against you and your king.

title: Samuel asks Israel to witness the sign and know their sin
speaker: Samuel
note: 12:17 completes the call: ‘Know and see that the evil you have done… is great.’

title: Israel asks Samuel to pray for them after the thunder
speaker: all the people
note: Distinct from the earlier request (ot-1-samuel-v7-8); they confess the sin of asking for a king.

title: Ceasing to pray for God’s people would be sin against the Lord
speaker: Samuel
note: Samuel’s commitment to intercede and teach the good way, stated as a principle; personal statement, hence low.

title: Samuel urges Israel to fear and serve the Lord or perish
speaker: Samuel
note: 12:25 attaches the warning: if you do evil, you and your king will be swept away.

title: Jonathan plans their approach and sets the condition for staying
speaker: Jonathan
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 14:8 (‘We will cross to the men’) opens the plan of 14:8–10.

title: Saul orders a muster to find who has left the camp
speaker: Saul
note: The muster shows that Jonathan and his armour-bearer are missing.

title: Saul calls for the ephod, then tells the priest to withdraw
speaker: Saul
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 14:19: Saul breaks off the inquiry (‘Withdraw your hands’) as the tumult grows.

title: Saul puts the army under oath not to eat before evening
speaker: King Saul
note: Royal oath-decree (‘Cursed is the man who eats bread’), restated at 14:28 (link); it leads to Jonathan’s condemnation.

title: Saul has a stone rolled up for slaughter without blood
speaker: Saul
note: Outside candidate list. 14:33 ‘Roll a large stone here to me’ begins the order. Candidates 14:28–29 fall under P00700.

title: Saul summons the chiefs and swears the offender must die
speaker: Saul
note: 14:39 binds the inquiry by oath: even Jonathan must die. 14:37 and 14:41 are inquiries addressed to God.

title: The people refuse Jonathan’s execution and rescue him by oath
speaker: the people
note: Collective oath overriding Saul’s sentence (ot-1-samuel-v14-44): ‘not one hair of his head shall fall’.

title: Samuel recalls Saul’s anointing and mission and rebukes his disobedience
speaker: Samuel
note: 15:17 and 15:19 frame the recalled mission: anointed though small, why did you not obey?

title: Samuel teaches Saul that obedience is better than sacrifice
speaker: Samuel
note: Outside candidate list. 15:23 completes the saying: divination is sin, and rejecting the Lord’s word costs the kingship.

title: Saul asks Samuel to pardon his sin and return with him
speaker: Saul
note: First plea, refused (15:26); the second plea is recorded at 15:30.

title: Saul orders his servants to find him a skilled musician
speaker: Saul
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Saul acts on his servants’ recorded proposal (16:16); it leads to David’s summons (16:19).

title: Saul asks Jesse to let David remain in his service
speaker: Saul
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: A second request to Jesse, after the recorded summons (16:19).

title: Goliath challenges Israel to send a champion, staking servitude
speaker: Goliath
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 17:9 sets the terms of the challenge: the loser’s people serve the winner’s.

title: The Lord saves not by sword and spear; the battle is his
speaker: David
note: 17:45 and 17:47 are outside the candidate list; candidate 17:46 is defiance and prediction. Compare ot-2-chronicles-v20-15.

title: Saul removes David and appoints him commander of a thousand
speaker: Saul
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported appointment, made out of fear (18:12); the catalogue records other narrated appointments (AUD-11-4-7).

title: Saul demands a hundred Philistine foreskins as David’s bride-price
speaker: Saul
note: Order to his servants carrying a deadly bride-price; David fulfils it (18:27).

title: Jonathan warns David to hide and promises to sound out Saul
speaker: Jonathan
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 19:3 completes Jonathan’s instruction: he will speak to Saul in the field and report back.

title: Jonathan pleads for David, and Saul swears not to kill him
speaker: Jonathan; Saul replies
note: 19:5 completes the plea; 19:6 records Saul’s oath ‘he shall not die’, soon broken (19:10).

title: Saul sends men to watch David’s house and kill him at dawn
speaker: Saul
note: Reported order preceding the recorded 19:15 order; Michal’s warning in the same verse is a separate finding.

title: Michal warns David to escape that night or be killed
speaker: Michal
note: Urgent warning like Jonathan’s (ot-1-samuel-v19-2); she lowers him through the window (19:12).

title: David asks Jonathan to cover his absence from the new-moon feast
speaker: David
note: 20:6 gives the excuse Jonathan is to tell Saul (delivered at 20:28–29); 20:7 sets the test of Saul’s reaction.

title: Jonathan asks David to show lasting kindness to his family
speaker: Jonathan
note: The request begins at 20:14 (‘you shall show mercy to me’) and closes with Jonathan’s renewed oath (20:16–17).

title: Jonathan explains which arrow signal means safety or flight
speaker: Jonathan
note: Outside candidate list. 20:22 gives the danger signal: ‘the shaft is beyond you… go’.

title: Jonathan sends the boy after the arrows to signal David
speaker: Jonathan
recipient: the little boy (and David hidden nearby)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 20:36 ‘Run, find the shafts’ and 20:37 ‘the shaft is beyond you’ belong to the same signal sequence.

title: David asks Abimelech for bread and receives the holy loaves
speaker: David; Abimelech the priest replies
note: The priest’s purity condition (21:5) bears on C0706; Jesus cites this episode at Mark 2:25–26 (K013).

title: Achish rebukes his servants and bars the feigning David from his house
speaker: Achish king of Gath
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Royal refusal (‘This one shall not enter a house’) that secures David’s escape.

title: David asks Moab’s king to shelter his father and mother
speaker: David
topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
note: Care for his parents while he is a fugitive; the king grants it (22:4).

title: Saul sentences Abimelech’s house and orders the priests killed
speaker: King Saul
note: 22:16 pronounces the death sentence; 22:18 (outside candidate list) turns the order to Doeg after the guards refuse.

title: Saul summons all the people to besiege David at Keilah
speaker: Saul
note: Reported order. David’s inquiries of the Lord (23:10–11) are prayers, and the oracle answers give no direction.

title: Saul sends the Ziphites to pinpoint David’s hiding places
speaker: Saul
note: Follows their recorded invitation (23:20); Saul’s blessing (23:21) needs nothing.

title: A messenger urges Saul to come quickly against a Philistine raid
speaker: a messenger
note: The summons that turns Saul back from David at the Divided Rock (23:28).

title: David shows Saul the cloak flap and pleads his innocence
speaker: David
note: 24:10–11 are outside the candidate list. ‘Know and see…’; David leaves judgment to the Lord. Compare the 26:19–20 records.

title: From the lawless comes wrongdoing, as the ancient proverb says
speaker: David, quoting an ancient proverb
note: Quoted proverb from which David concludes, ‘my hand shall not be against you’.

summary: Judges 5–Ruth 4–1 Samuel 24: mostly unrecorded narrative orders, requests and oaths (Saul’s fasting oath, Israel’s Benjamin oath, Saul’s anointing, Ruth’s redemption request, two vows) plus extensions completing single-verse speech records.
